items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: The mention of 'Swanton' appears only in a parenthetical note by the interviewer/editor referencing a book ('Swanton, Indian Tribes of North America'), not in the interviewee's spoken narrative.

ctx.x: We had a jukebox on at intermission that had Gene Krupa on the jukebox. Freddie would listen to this record for 20

*Butler's pronunciation, but probably meaning Caughnawaga, the name of a Mohawk village near Auriesville, New York, near Canada. (see Swanton, Indian Tribes of North America, Smithsonian Bulletin of Amer. Ethnology, #145.

minutes then one night he says, you know Jacques, that man can't do nothing with me. I'm going to show you. He played the record, he got up on his drums and played with the record. He said, now, you see? You see what I did to him, don't you? I said, yeah, Freddie, you got it.
